doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Songwriting craft and technology; changing audience tastes
summary: Rowe and Wolff discuss how technology affects songwriting and how tastes mature with age.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: I think too that the craft that it took to sit at a piano and write those tunes, when you have technology into the mix these days, sometimes you tend to depend too much on the technology and perhaps the chord structures don’t have to be as sophisticated because you have this interesting drum sound from a machine. I think there is great songs written today but the focus is a little different.

It is indeed and I think the audience will change as this audience today gets older. We may see people today enjoying a kind of music that you and I aren’t turned on to. I think these are the very same people who five, ten years from now will enjoy the kind of music we enjoy today. So I think it’s a question sometimes of growing up and maturity as well as exposure.
